grade_reason: No statement by him about AI since 1 January 2025 was found in seven web searches or in his official press releases from December 2024 to October 2026.
notes: All 7 web searches ran this time (the 6 required plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act). None returned a statement by him on AI since 2025. The official-site search found only older AI items, both outside the date range: his February 2024 appointment to the House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence (https://dunn.house.gov/2024/2/congressman-dunn-appointed-to-the-house-task-force-on-artificial-intelligence) and a 2019 defense bill amendment requiring a Defense Department report on its AI use (https://dunn.house.gov/2019/7/dunn-artificial-intelligence-amendment-included-in-defense-authorization-bill); he is also listed as a member in the task force's December 2024 final report. The search on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (Sanders and Casar, September 2026) found no source naming him as a co-sponsor; congress.gov co-sponsor lists were not opened directly. From the earlier attempt (still valid): dunn.house.gov press release listing pages 1 to 4 (https://dunn.house.gov/news/documentquery.aspx?DocumentTypeID=27, 9 December 2024 to 2 October 2026) and the In the News page were checked, and no release title or excerpt mentions AI; excerpts are truncated, so not every full text was read. His issues pages have no technology or AI section. Energy and Commerce hearing remarks (he is a vice chair of the committee) and floor speeches were not searched individually. His 13 January 2026 press release says he is not seeking re-election, so he leaves the House on 3 January 2027.
